title: [CQ-R08] Scoped host guest bridge
description:
Objective: Use fixed-command bounded stdio framing for task-scoped agent requests and supervisor-only observations.

Deliverable: Scoped host guest bridge. This is task R08 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): R07, F06.

implementationPlan.description: Create the host-only session entry point with inline contract documentation: runGuestSession({name,binding,sessionId,daemonInfoPath,forward,onOutput,onObservation,signal,provider={},timeoutMs=30000}). provider supplies executable (default multipass) and spawn (default node:child_process spawn); forward(tool,args,{signal}) is the mandatory trusted host daemon transport returning an MCP tool-result JSON value. Require all three callbacks, validate timeoutMs as a positive safe integer <=60000, validate sessionId verbatim as nonblank <=255 UTF-16 units without NUL/CR/LF, validate the executable using the existing invoker convention, and require an absolute native-host daemonInfoPath. Snapshot/freeze the binding and validate it through scopeRequest on a harmless synthetic get_context request (no dispatch); use bridgeArgv(name) unchanged. Bounded-read at most 16 KiB plus an overflow sentinel from a regular daemon-info file, closing the file on every path; fail on missing/read/parse/shape errors. Admit only an absent own bindHost (daemon's default) or literal 127.0.0.1/::1; no DNS resolution, environment fallback, wildcard, coercion or WSL exception. Perform this guard before spawning and again before each actual forward. Spawn only the fixed bridgeArgv command with shell:false, windowsHide:true and piped stdin/stdout/stderr; no host daemon address/token/settings in the guest argv or env additions. Consume stdout using the existing decoder/parseGuestFrame; require hello first exactly once, strictly increasing request IDs (one last-ID counter, no growing replay set), and one terminal exit observation. Child output goes only to onOutput(stream,Buffer), never to a decoder or dispatcher. Drain/discard provider stderr without collecting or exposing it. Deliver onObservation and resolve {observation,executionReady:false} only after clean decoder EOF, provider close code 0/no signal, exactly one observation and no outstanding replies; a nonzero observed job exit is real data, not transport success of the job. No activation or readiness claim.

Error handling and bounded forwarding: Complete bounded forwarding and teardown. Keep stdout pumping independently while servicing requests serially, with at most 64 queued+active requests; excess, protocol violations or read failures end the session, never accumulate an unbounded queue. For each request call scopeRequest unchanged, reject argument trees deeper than 64 with a small iterative traversal before daemon dispatch, and catch serialization/send exceptions including RangeError. After scoping, stamp host sessionId onto get_context, and host attemptId/generation/sessionId onto start_step, complete_step and complete_task only; never stamp unsupported fields on heartbeat/get_handoff_history/QA tools. Policy/depth refusals receive exactly one response with the original supervisor ID and fixed error code, with zero forward calls. A forward rejection or MCP isError result gets only BRIDGE_UPSTREAM_FAILED (no exception/message/result echo); otherwise wrap the JSON tool result in {kind:'response',id,ok:true,result}. Encode responses with a conservative 1 MiB limit, leaving headroom for Python re-encoding below its 4 MiB cap; unencodable/oversize results get one small BRIDGE_RESPONSE_INVALID response. Serialize stdin writes and await their completion/backpressure while stdout continues; bound hello, each forward and each write by timeoutMs. Never retry mutations. On timeout or abort terminate the session, abort the per-session signal, ignore late results, and prevent post-close writes/callbacks/unhandled rejections. One idempotent cleanup path handles every terminal event: stop admitting/dispatching, close stdin to let the supervisor's host-EOF path reap the group, continue draining stdout, and wait at most timeoutMs before killing only the local spawned provider as fallback; clear timers and detach operational listeners safely. Any forced/unknown teardown remains failure and never produces a fabricated observation or proof of guest termination. All surfaced errors use fixed allowlisted codes/messages without caller values, paths or diagnostics. Finish the H-series assertions against each branch; no new wire kinds or edits to guest-bridge/supervisor.

implementationPlan.description: Add one bounded real-Python end-to-end H test using the existing LOAD/PEER/SUPERVISOR conventions and python3 -I -B. Inject spawn only to replace the fixed Multipass launch with the actual supervisor relay harness; still assert the production executable/argv/options passed to it. The actual child connects to relay's agent socket, sends an allowed request plus forbidden role/settings/dependency/foreign-identity requests, receives precisely correlated success/refusal frames, writes binary stdout containing forged hello/request/exit frames, and exits with a chosen nonzero code. Run the new JS host session, not the old manual answering helper: assert forward sees only the scoped allowed call with host session identity, forged bytes are delivered byte-for-byte solely as output, and only waitpid's real exit reaches onObservation. Exercise a silent real child with host abort as well: stdin EOF terminates/reaps it and removes its socket; keep finally/after cleanup for assertion failures. Use 30-second test deadlines and existing explicit win32 skip; Linux exercises real SO_PEERCRED, macOS uses PEER injection. A non-loopback daemon fixture must prevent even starting this harness. Document in test/entry-point comments that these are real local supervisor integration tests, not live VM or network-isolation certification; defer the epic docs sweep and native probes to R13.
implementationPlan.note:
Added H5, one real-Python end-to-end test, with { skip: NO_GUEST, timeout: 30_000 }. Off Linux it uses PEER injection; Linux uses the real SO_PEERCRED.

Harness:
- supervised(job, ...args) is the injected spawn. It records the production launch, which H5 asserts equals SPAWNED: 'multipass', bridgeArgv(NAME), {shell:false, windowsHide:true, three pipes}.
- It then runs `python3 -I -B -c LOAD+relay(..., agent_socket, agent_uid=os.getuid()) guest-supervisor.py` with those same options, creating the socket dir only at spawn.
- It joins the existing `sessions` after() cleanup, which kills the job and supervisor and removes the dir.
- The new JS runGuestSession drives it; the old manual answering helper is not used.

Coverage:
1. A daemon.json with bindHost 0.0.0.0 gives SESSION_DAEMON_NOT_LOOPBACK, and the harness is never launched (launches=[]).
2. The real agent job connects to the socket and sends 5 requests with ids 40-44:
   - get_context {} is the allowed call;
   - role qa, init_project (settings), set_task_dependencies and a foreign workerId are the forbidden ones.
   It writes each answer to stderr, writes binary stdout (forged HELLO, REQUEST and EXIT frames plus 00 ff 0a), and exits 3.
3. Assertions:
   - forward saw exactly [get_context {taskId, workerId, sessionId: host SESSION_ID}];
   - stdout output equals the forged bytes byte for byte;
   - the agent got answered(40) and then refusals 41 IDENTITY_MISMATCH, 42/43 TOOL_DENIED and 44 IDENTITY_MISMATCH, each under its own id;
   - the observation is the waitpid exit {code 3};
   - the supervisor exited 0 and the socket is removed.
4. Silent job plus abort: the session closes stdin, the supervisor exits 74, and the job is dead and reaped. The socket is gone, there is no observation and no local kill.
The comments state these are local processes, not VM/Multipass/network certification (CQ-R13).

comments.author: architect-26ba32c3
comments.content:
Split on 2026-10-25 (architect-26ba32c3). The full bridge measured at about 650 net LOC: a host codec and scoping module, a guest supervisor in Python (the guest has python3 but no Node), a host session, and tests. That is far over the 400-net-LOC QA limit, and no rail waives it. Following this epic's M01 and C02 pattern, this row keeps its full DoD and becomes the final slice, depending on:
- CQ-R08a task-f981d059 (PLANNING): scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs, which is the frame protocol, guest frame schema, per-role request scoping and fixed bridgeArgv. Tests go in the new scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, registered in CI.
- CQ-R08b task-502c00a5 (BACKLOG): scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py, a stdlib-only supervisor that is the sole writer of its stdout. It relays child output only as base64 output frames and reports exit only from its own waitpid.
- CQ-R08c task-10e201f9 (BACKLOG): the agent request ingress, a Unix socket that admits only the moe-agent peer uid, assigns its own ids, and routes each response back to the requester only.

What remains for this row, to plan once the three slices land:
- The host bridge session: run bridgeArgv through the R06 invoker style with an injected spawn, require hello first, pump frames, and pass each request through scopeRequest and an injected forward. Bound in-flight requests and time them out, deliver output and observations to callbacks, and fail closed by killing the child on any violation.
- A loopback-only daemon guard: refuse to open when `.moe/daemon.json` records a non-loopback bindHost. That is WSL agent mode's 0.0.0.0, which a Multipass guest could reach through its gateway.
- An end-to-end test between the JS session and the real Python supervisor that proves DoD 1-3.
Verification: `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs`. It is a superset of the DoD command, so local-runner.test.mjs, which R04 and R05 also edit, is never touched.

comments.author: worker-c1d9de02
comments.content:
Handoff from CQ-R08a (task-f981d0597b26401a974c0fcd8829107e, guest-bridge.mjs). This is a requirement for the CQ-R08 forwarding path, not a defect in R08a.

1. Deeply nested args. parseGuestFrame and scopeRequest enforce exact keys and allowlists but no nesting depth. A guest frame within 256 KiB can carry about 100k levels of nesting in an allowed arg value, and JSON.parse accepts it. Re-serializing such a value can throw RangeError (stack overflow). encodeFrame already catches that and returns BRIDGE_FRAME_INVALID, but the CQ-R08 forwarding must catch JSON.stringify/send errors too, or bound the depth before forwarding, so a guest cannot crash the host session or the daemon.
2. Duplicate JSON keys. JS JSON.parse keeps the last occurrence of a duplicate key, and Python json does too by default. The R08b/c supervisor should not rely on first-wins.
3. Lost frames on error. Any decoder error poisons it, and any frames already decoded in the same push are discarded. The session should treat a throw as teardown.

comments.author: qa-b0c1741e
comments.content: QA note from the CQ-R08a review, for planning CQ-R08. guest-bridge.mjs TOOLS (in 17bc7ac) matches every committed daemon inputSchema. However, the uncommitted CQ-F06 edit (task-b03c0c7744e84955a7a069255a124ef7, Served context identity) adds a `sessionId` property to the moe.get_context schema. Today a guest-sent sessionId gets BRIDGE_ARGUMENT_DENIED, which fails closed. Once F06 lands, CQ-R08 should decide explicitly between two options: stamp a host-owned sessionId from the binding (preferred, since a receipt binds to the owning attempt), or keep refusing it. It should not add sessionId to the guest argument allowlist without a decision. Also note the B9 pin in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, which any table change must update.

comments.author: worker-7d158765
comments.content:
CQ-R08b (task-502c00a5) handoff: two gaps in the guest-supervisor relay that belong downstream, not in R08b.
1. A silent child and a host that has gone: the relay notices only on its next frame write (EPIPE → exit 74, then killpg+reap). CQ-R08c should put stdin (host frames) in the same selectors loop, so host EOF ends the session promptly.
2. A SIGTERM or SIGHUP sent to the supervisor uses the default action and kills Python without running the finally. The child's session group (start_new_session) then survives. Only KeyboardInterrupt/OSError paths kill and reap today. Signal-driven teardown belongs to CQ-R08 or CQ-R10/R11.
Exit-code contract for the host session: 0 relay complete; 64 usage; 71 child failed to start (hello, then EOF, no observation); 74 I/O failure (child group killed); 77 not root; 78 root with no job. relay also resets SIGCHLD to SIG_DFL, because an inherited SIG_IGN would let the kernel discard the status before waitpid reads it.

2. Role or worker substitution gives IDENTITY_MISMATCH; settings and dependency tools give TOOL_DENIED; the binding is snapshotted (H3, H5).
3. Forged frames on child stdout stay byte-exact output; the exit comes only from waitpid (H5).
